Health and wellbeing outcome measures are used to compare treatments and to
inform how health budgets are allocated. Several established instruments exist,
and they do not always agree with each other about the same person. Where
mapping functions convert between them, those functions are usually estimated
on one survey sample and then applied elsewhere.

This project uses the SIPHER-HWMIC survey, which asked over 12,000 UK adults
the questions from eight different health and wellbeing instruments, across
three separate survey panels.

What the project will involve:

- comparing scores from several preference-based instruments for the same respondents
- testing whether mapping between instruments holds when trained on one survey panel and applied to another
- reporting calibration as well as fit, the external-validation approach standard in clinical prediction modelling but uncommon in this literature
- examining whether disagreement between instruments varies systematically by age, sex, socioeconomic position or health status
- handling documented data quality problems in the survey and reporting to the MAPS statement, the mapping literature's own reporting standard
